title: One row per order
prompt: The ingestion job sometimes delivers the same order or the same customer twice. Finance needs each order exactly once, with its customer's name. Write `solve(orders, customers)` so it returns `order_id`, `customer_id`, `name` and `total`.
rules: A row delivered twice is an exact copy of another row in the same table. Remove copies from both tables.
Different orders can share a customer and have the same total; they are not copies. Each distinct order row appears once.
An order whose customer isn't in `customers` stays, with a missing `name`. Return only these four columns, in this order.
hints: Copies on either side multiply rows. Check each input before joining.
`dropDuplicates()` with no arguments removes exact copies only. Deduplicating on `customer_id` would remove real orders.
Use a join that keeps every order, then select the four columns.
